question: In an Alabama CDL air brake system, at what pressure is the safety relief valve usually set to open?
choice_a: 125 psi
choice_b: 100 psi
choice_c: 150 psi
choice_d: 200 psi
explanation: The safety valve, installed in the first tank the air compressor pumps air to, is usually set to open at 150 psi to protect the tank and the rest of the system from too much pressure.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-1

question: What is the purpose of an alcohol evaporator in some air brake systems?
choice_a: To lubricate the air compressor
choice_b: To put alcohol into the air system to reduce the risk of ice in air brake valves during cold weather
choice_c: To cool the compressed air before it enters the tanks
choice_d: To measure the amount of moisture in the air tanks
explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator that puts alcohol into the air system, which helps reduce the risk of ice forming in air brake valves and other parts during cold weather, since ice inside the system can make the brakes stop working.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-1

question: What is the most common type of foundation brake used at each wheel on air-braked commercial vehicles?
choice_a: Wedge brake
choice_b: Modulating drum brake
choice_c: Disc brake
choice_d: S-cam drum brake
explanation: Foundation brakes are used at each wheel, and the most common type is the s-cam drum brake.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-1

question: In an s-cam drum brake, what happens as the slack adjuster moves after the brake pedal is pushed?
choice_a: It twists the brake camshaft, which turns the s-cam and forces the brake shoes apart against the drum
choice_b: It releases air from the tank directly to the atmosphere
choice_c: It pushes a wedge directly between the brake shoes
choice_d: It clamps the brake rotor between lining pads with a power screw
explanation: When the brake pedal is pushed, air pressure pushes the rod out, moving the slack adjuster and twisting the camshaft, which turns the s-cam so it forces the brake shoes apart and presses them against the inside of the brake drum.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-1

question: How do wedge brakes force the brake shoes against the drum?
choice_a: A slack adjuster rotates an s-cam to force the shoes apart
choice_b: The brake chamber push rod pushes a wedge directly between the ends of two brake shoes, shoving them apart against the drum
choice_c: Spring pressure alone forces the shoes against the drum
choice_d: A power screw clamps the shoes against the drum like a c-clamp
explanation: In wedge brakes, the brake chamber push rod pushes a wedge directly between the ends of two brake shoes, which shoves them apart and against the inside of the brake drum.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-1

question: What component does an air-operated disc brake use in place of the s-cam found in s-cam drum brakes?
choice_a: An alcohol evaporator
choice_b: A power screw
choice_c: A wedge
choice_d: A modulating valve
explanation: In air-operated disc brakes, the pressure of the brake chamber on the slack adjuster turns a "power screw," which clamps the disc or rotor between the brake lining pads of a caliper, similar to a large c-clamp, instead of using an s-cam.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-1

question: On some older vehicles (made before 1975) equipped with a front brake limiting valve, what happens when the cab control is placed in the "slippery" position?
choice_a: It cuts the normal air pressure to the front brakes by half
choice_b: It doubles the air pressure to the front brakes
choice_c: It shuts off the front brakes entirely
choice_d: It applies the front spring brakes
explanation: Placing the front brake limiting valve control in the "slippery" position cuts the normal air pressure to the front brakes by half; the manual notes these valves actually reduce the vehicle's stopping power and the control should normally be kept in the "normal" position.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-2

question: What does the supply pressure gauge on an air brake vehicle show the driver?
choice_a: The rate of air leakage in the system
choice_b: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes right now
choice_c: How much pressure is in the air tanks
choice_d: The temperature of the compressed air
explanation: All vehicles with air brakes have a pressure gauge connected to the air tank, and these gauges tell the driver how much pressure is in the air tanks.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-1

question: On a vehicle equipped with an application pressure gauge, what does it mean if you need increasing application pressure to hold the same speed?
choice_a: The dual air system has switched to the secondary circuit
choice_b: The parking brakes are engaged
choice_c: The brakes are fading, and you should slow down and use a lower gear
choice_d: The alcohol evaporator needs refilling
explanation: Needing increasing application pressure to hold the same speed means the brakes are fading; the driver should slow down and use a lower gear, since the cause can also be brakes out of adjustment, air leaks, or mechanical problems.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-2

question: A visible low air pressure warning signal on an air brake vehicle must come on before the air pressure in the tanks falls below what level?
choice_a: 45 psi
choice_b: 65 psi
choice_c: 55 psi
choice_d: 100 psi
explanation: A low air pressure warning signal you can see must come on before the air pressure in the tanks falls below 55 psi (or one half the compressor governor cutout pressure on older vehicles).
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-2

question: How does an automatic "wig wag" low air pressure warning device behave?
choice_a: It permanently locks the brakes when pressure is low
choice_b: It sounds a buzzer only, with no visual signal
choice_c: It drops a mechanical arm into view when pressure drops below 55 psi and rises out of view when pressure rises above 55 psi
choice_d: It only works on vehicles with dual air systems
explanation: The wig wag drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when system pressure drops below 55 psi; an automatic wig wag rises out of view again once pressure goes back above 55 psi.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-2

question: On large buses, at what pressure range is it common for the low pressure warning devices to signal?
choice_d: 55 psi
explanation: The manual notes that on large buses it is common for the low pressure warning devices to signal at 80-85 psi.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-2

question: Why are spring brakes typically used for the emergency and parking brakes on trucks, truck tractors, and buses?
choice_a: Because air pressure can eventually leak away, and parking/emergency brakes must be held on by mechanical force
choice_b: Because they are required only on vehicles equipped with ABS
choice_c: Because they provide a smoother stop than service brakes
choice_d: Because they are cheaper to install than air-only brakes
explanation: Trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency and parking brakes held on by mechanical force because air pressure can eventually leak away; spring brakes, held back by air pressure while driving, are usually used to meet this need.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-2

question: On a tractor or straight truck, spring brakes will come fully on when air pressure drops into what range?
choice_a: 20 to 45 psi
choice_b: 50 to 65 psi
choice_c: 70 to 90 psi
choice_d: 5 to 15 psi
explanation: Tractor and straight truck spring brakes come fully on when air pressure drops into a range of 20 to 45 psi (typically 20 to 30 psi); drivers should not wait for this and should stop safely as soon as the low air warning light and buzzer first come on.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-2

question: On newer vehicles, what does the driver use to apply the parking (spring) brakes?
choice_a: A diamond-shaped, yellow, push-pull control knob
choice_b: A foot-operated treadle valve
choice_c: A dash-mounted modulating lever only
choice_d: A round blue knob
explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the driver puts on the parking brakes using a diamond-shaped, yellow, push-pull control knob, pulling it out to apply the spring brakes and pushing it in to release them.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-2

question: Why should a driver never push the brake pedal down while the spring brakes are on?
choice_a: It has no effect since spring brakes override the pedal
choice_b: The brakes could be damaged by the combined forces of the springs and the air pressure
choice_c: It will drain the alcohol evaporator
choice_d: It will trigger the ABS malfunction lamp
explanation: The manual warns that pushing the brake pedal down while the spring brakes are on could damage the brakes from the combined forces of the springs and the air pressure, so drivers should develop the habit of not doing this even though some systems are designed to prevent it.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-2

question: When should a driver avoid using the parking brakes, according to the manual?
choice_a: When the brakes are very hot from a steep grade, or very wet in freezing temperatures
choice_b: Whenever driving in dual air brake mode
choice_c: When the vehicle is fully loaded
choice_d: Whenever the ABS malfunction lamp is on
explanation: The manual advises against using the parking brakes if the brakes are very hot, such as after coming down a steep grade, since the heat can damage them, or if they are very wet in freezing temperatures, since they could freeze and prevent the vehicle from moving.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-8

question: Under the requirements described in the manual, truck tractors with air brakes built on or after what date must be equipped with antilock brakes?
choice_a: March 1, 1998
choice_b: March 1, 1997
choice_c: January 1, 1995
choice_d: January 1, 2000
explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 are required to be equipped with antilock brakes, while other air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) must have ABS if built on or after March 1, 1998.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-3

question: Where are the yellow ABS malfunction lamps located on trailers?
choice_a: Centered on the rear bumper
choice_b: On the instrument panel
choice_c: On the left side, either the front or rear corner
choice_d: Inside the cab only
explanation: Trailers have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner, while tractors, trucks, and buses have theirs on the instrument panel.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-3

question: According to the manual, what effect does ABS have on a vehicle's normal braking capability?
choice_a: It replaces the need for spring brakes
choice_b: It increases normal stopping power at all times
choice_c: It does not decrease or increase normal braking capability; it only activates when wheels are about to lock up
choice_d: It decreases normal stopping power to help prevent skids
explanation: ABS is an addition to normal brakes that does not decrease or increase normal braking capability; it only activates when the wheels are about to lock up, and it does not necessarily shorten stopping distance but does help keep the vehicle under control during hard braking.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-3

question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, how much minimum air pressure should be allowed to build up in both the primary and secondary systems?
choice_a: 125 psi
choice_b: 100 psi
choice_c: 55 psi
choice_d: 80 psi
explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, the driver should allow time for the air compressor to build up a minimum of 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-4

question: In a dual air brake system, the low air pressure warning light and buzzer must come on before the air pressure drops below what level in either system?
choice_a: 75 psi
choice_b: 100 psi
choice_c: 55 psi
choice_d: 45 psi
explanation: In a dual air system, the warning light and buzzer should come on before the air pressure drops below 55 psi in either the primary or secondary system.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-4

question: When checking slack adjusters on s-cam brakes during a walk-around inspection, what amount of movement at the push rod attachment point suggests the slack adjuster needs adjustment?
choice_a: Movement of more than about one inch
choice_b: Movement of more than about six inches
choice_c: Any visible movement at all
choice_d: Movement of more than about three feet
explanation: After parking on level ground, chocking the wheels, and releasing the parking brakes, if a slack adjuster moves more than about one inch where the push rod attaches to it, it probably needs adjustment; out-of-adjustment brakes are the most common problem found in roadside inspections.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-5

question: During the Step 7 final air brake check, at approximately what pressure should the air compressor start pumping, and at what pressure should it cut out?
choice_a: Start at about 55 psi, cut out at about 100 psi
choice_b: Start at about 150 psi, cut out at about 200 psi
choice_c: Start at about 100 psi, cut out at about 125 psi
choice_d: Start at about 125 psi, cut out at about 150 psi
explanation: When checking the air compressor governor cut-in and cut-out pressures, pumping by the air compressor should start at about 100 psi and stop (cut out) at about 125 psi.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-6

question: When testing the static air leakage rate with a fully charged system and the parking brake released, what is the maximum acceptable loss rate for a single vehicle?
choice_a: Less than 4 psi in one minute
choice_b: Less than 6 psi in one minute
choice_c: Less than 2 psi in one minute
choice_d: Less than 1 psi in one minute
explanation: With a fully-charged air system, the loss rate should be less than two psi in one minute for single vehicles, and less than three psi in one minute for combination vehicles.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-6

question: What is the correct sequence for the "stab braking" emergency stopping method?
choice_a: Pump the brakes rapidly and continuously without fully releasing
choice_b: Apply the brakes lightly, then gradually increase pressure until stopped
choice_c: Apply the parking brake first, then the service brakes
choice_d: Apply the brakes all the way, release when the wheels lock up, and reapply fully as soon as the wheels start rolling again
explanation: With stab braking, the driver applies the brakes all the way, releases them when the wheels lock up, and applies them fully again as soon as the wheels start rolling, since it can take up to one second for the wheels to start rolling after release.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-7

question: About how much distance does air brake lag add at 55 mph on dry pavement, contributing to a total stopping distance of over 450 feet under good conditions?
choice_a: About 32 feet
choice_b: About 12 feet
choice_c: About 100 feet
choice_d: About 55 feet
explanation: The air brake lag distance at 55 mph on dry pavement adds about 32 feet, so for an average driver under good traction and brake conditions, the total stopping distance at that speed is over 450 feet.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-7

question: What primarily causes "brake fade," which with continued overuse can reduce a vehicle's ability to slow or stop?
choice_a: Excessive use of the service brakes causing overheating, which leads to chemical changes in the brake lining and expansion of the brake drums
choice_b: Using the parking brake too frequently while driving on flat roads
choice_c: Keeping the front brake limiting valve in the "normal" position
choice_d: Running the alcohol evaporator dry in warm weather
explanation: Excessive use of the service brakes results in overheating and brake fade; the excessive heat causes chemical changes in the brake lining that reduce friction and causes the brake drums to expand, so the shoes and linings must travel farther and the force of contact is reduced.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-8
